question: Which canonical skill capability format and staged trust model should OpenClaw and ClawHub support: existing SKILL.md metadata or a separate signed manifest, and when should declarations become enforceable?
rationale: This determines a public ecosystem schema, upgrade behavior, user-consent semantics, runtime authorization boundaries, and the meaning of signing and trust indicators; source inspection cannot safely choose those policies without maintainer intent.

options.title: Extend SKILL.md in phases
options.body: Standardize capabilities in existing metadata, ship inspection and update-diff visibility first, then add explicit consent and opt-in enforcement before considering stricter defaults.

options.title: Adopt a separate signed manifest
options.body: Define skill.yaml as authoritative with explicit precedence, migration, signature scope, and compatibility rules for existing skills.

options.title: Keep registry analysis only
options.body: Limit declarations and trust scoring to ClawHub while installed skills remain governed by existing agent, tool, sandbox, and plugin policies.

recommendation.title: Extend SKILL.md in phases
recommendation.body: Standardize capabilities in existing metadata, ship inspection and update-diff visibility first, then add explicit consent and opt-in enforcement before considering stricter defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the explicit product and security keep-open direction and are connected to the vision and documentation boundaries that require a decision.
